tagline: The French Riviera of the East · Eco-Heritage Coastal Haven

places.name: Sri Aurobindo Ashram
places.review_summary: Peaceful spiritual sanctuary and meditation courtyard housing the Samadhi.

guidelines.dress_code: Modest attire covering shoulders and knees; footwear must be deposited at entry.
guidelines.photography: Strictly prohibited inside the courtyard and samadhi.
guidelines.accessibility: Wheelchair ramp available at main gate.

places.shortDescription: Peaceful spiritual sanctuary and meditation courtyard housing the Samadhi.
places.longDescription: Founded by Sri Aurobindo and The Mother, this spiritual community occupies a former French colonial house on Rue de la Marine in White Town. The centrepiece is the flower-covered Samadhi, a marble tomb in a serene meditation courtyard. Visitors can explore the main building, the Ashram Library, and quiet reading rooms. Photography is strictly prohibited inside the courtyard and samadhi area, maintaining the contemplative atmosphere that draws seekers from around the world.
whatToExperience: Silent meditation at the flower-covered Samadhi
places.accessNote: Photography prohibited inside courtyard and samadhi area. Modest attire required.

places.name: White Town (French Quarter)
places.review_summary: Colonial pastel villas, mustard façades, bougainvillea gates and French street signs.

guidelines.dress_code: Casual, comfortable walking attire; breathable linen recommended.
guidelines.photography: Permitted for personal photography; respect residential privacy.

places.shortDescription: Colonial pastel villas, mustard façades, bougainvillea gates and French street signs.
places.longDescription: White Town is a charming grid of pastel-coloured French colonial villas situated east of the canal that divides Pondicherry. Streets such as Rue Dumas, Rue Romain Rolland, and Rue Suffren feature bougainvillea-draped walls, wrought-iron gates, and distinctive mustard-and-cream façades. The neighbourhood preserves its Franco-Tamil architectural character and is best explored on foot or by bicycle in the early morning when the light is soft and traffic is minimal.
places.accessNote: Best explored on foot or bicycle. Respect residential privacy.

places.name: Promenade Beach (Rock Beach)
places.review_summary: 1.5 km coastal promenade along basalt seawall with ocean vistas and evening sea breeze.

guidelines.dress_code: Casual beachside attire; no swimming due to treacherous rocky coast.
guidelines.accessibility: Wide pedestrian boulevard, level ramps at Gandhi Statue.

places.shortDescription: 1.5 km coastal promenade along basalt seawall with ocean vistas and evening sea breeze.
places.longDescription: Promenade Beach, also known as Rock Beach, is a 1.5 km stretch along Goubert Avenue running from the War Memorial to the Dupleix statue. A paved pedestrian boulevard lined with heritage buildings offers unobstructed sunrise views over the Bay of Bengal. Landmarks along the route include the Gandhi statue and the old lighthouse. The rocky coastline makes swimming unsafe, but evening crowds gather for the sea breeze and street-food stalls. Vehicles are banned on the promenade during evenings.
whatToExperience: Gandhi statue and Gingee pillars viewing
Evening sea breeze and food stalls
places.accessNote: No swimming due to rocky coast. Vehicles banned 6 PM - 7:30 AM.

places.name: Pondicherry Museum
places.review_summary: Sheltered galleries displaying Arikamedu Roman trade relics and French colonial transport.

guidelines.photography: Permitted without flash; additional nominal fee for camera.

places.shortDescription: Sheltered galleries displaying Arikamedu Roman trade relics and French colonial transport.
places.longDescription: Housed in a colonial-era building on Rue Saint Louis, the Pondicherry Museum showcases the region's layered history through diverse galleries. Highlights include archaeological artefacts from Arikamedu, the ancient Roman trade settlement, alongside geological specimens, stone sculptures, and French colonial-era transport exhibits. Additional sections cover Pondicherry's cultural evolution from its pre-colonial past through the French administration period, offering a compact overview of the territory's heritage.
places.accessNote: Closed on Mondays and national holidays.

places.name: Matrimandir Viewing Point & Gardens
places.review_summary: Iconic golden geodesic sphere set amidst 12 peaceful meditation gardens.

guidelines.dress_code: Modest attire required; quiet contemplation observed.
guidelines.entry_fee: Free (Free pass issued at Visitor Centre)
guidelines.photography: Permitted from outside viewing point only.

places.shortDescription: Iconic golden geodesic sphere set amidst 12 peaceful meditation gardens.
places.longDescription: The Matrimandir is a golden geodesic sphere in Auroville designed by architect Roger Anger as a place for silent concentration. Its inner chamber houses the largest optically perfect crystal globe in the world. Surrounding the structure are twelve petal-shaped meditation gardens, each representing a human aspiration such as sincerity, humility, and courage. Visitors can obtain a free viewing pass from the Auroville Visitors Centre and take an electric shuttle to the designated viewing area near the ancient banyan tree.
whatToExperience: Viewing the golden sphere from gardens
places.accessNote: Free viewing pass required from Auroville Visitors Centre. Electric shuttle available.

places.name: Casablanca Heritage Boutique
places.review_summary: Three floors of curated Pondicherry pottery, organic linen, leather goods & café.
places.shortDescription: Three floors of curated Pondicherry pottery, organic linen, leather goods & café.
places.longDescription: Casablanca is a multi-level lifestyle store located on Mission Street in Pondicherry, specialising in locally crafted pottery, handloom textiles, organic skincare products, and leather goods. Each floor showcases curated collections from regional artisans and sustainable brands. The building's colonial architecture adds character to the shopping experience. A rooftop café on the upper floor offers courtyard views and a relaxed spot for refreshments after browsing the store.
places.accessNote: Open daily. Café on upper floor.

places.name: Cluny Embroidery Centre
places.review_summary: 18th-century French convent workshop supporting underprivileged local craftswomen.
places.shortDescription: 18th-century French convent workshop supporting underprivileged local craftswomen.
places.longDescription: The Cluny Embroidery Centre is a heritage workshop housed inside a former French convent in Pondicherry. It supports underprivileged women artisans who produce exquisite hand-embroidered linen, table settings, and clothing using traditional French embroidery techniques passed down over generations. Visitors can observe the meticulous craftsmanship in action and purchase finished pieces directly from the workshop, supporting both the preservation of heritage skills and the livelihoods of local women.
places.accessNote: Closed Sundays and Mondays. Photography restricted inside studio.

places.name: Paradise Beach
places.shortDescription: Sandy, scenic and relaxed beach reached by ferry boat ride from Chunnambar Boat House.
places.longDescription: Paradise Beach is a secluded golden sand beach located south of Puducherry at the mouth of the Chunnambar backwaters. Fringed by quiet coastal casuarina groves and gentle surf, visitors usually arrive via a scenic 15-minute boat journey from Chunnambar Boat House. The shoreline offers a tranquil, unspoiled atmosphere for coastal strolls and sea breezes.
places.accessNote: Reached by boat from Chunnambar Boat House during ferry operational hours.
places.bestTime: Morning or mid-afternoon before last ferry

places.name: Serenity Beach
places.shortDescription: Scenic northern beach celebrated for sunrise vistas, surfing lessons, and vibrant fishing catamarans.
places.longDescription: Serenity Beach is situated north of Puducherry's town centre along the East Coast Road. Known for its picturesque rocky pier jutting out into the Bay of Bengal, it is a favourite spot for early morning sunrise photography, local fishing boats resting on golden sands, and beginner surf lessons.
whatToExperience: Sunrise over the Bay of Bengal
places.accessNote: Check sea conditions before swimming; active fishing zone.

places.name: Eden Beach
places.shortDescription: Certified clean coastal beach with managed visitor facilities and landscaped walkways.
places.longDescription: Eden Beach, located near Chinnaveerampattinam village, is an eco-managed beachfront recognized with international Blue Flag certification. It features clean sandbars, watchtowers, bamboo seating, solar-powered facilities, and clean washroom amenities in a protected natural setting.
places.accessNote: Managed beach with dedicated parking and strict anti-littering rules.

places.name: Pondy Marina Beach
places.shortDescription: Developed waterfront beach with wide sands, evening food stalls, and proximity to the New Lighthouse.
places.longDescription: Pondy Marina Beach is a lively urban coastal destination located near the modern New Lighthouse at the southern end of the city. Developed with landscaped boardwalks, seating pergolas, and a vibrant local food court offering regional coastal delicacies, it is popular for evening leisure.
places.accessNote: Lively in evenings; food court stalls operate primarily afternoon through night.

places.name: Auroville Beach
places.shortDescription: Quiet coastal stretch for peaceful walks, sunrise views, and gentle sea breezes north of town.
places.longDescription: Auroville Beach, commonly called Auro Beach, sits along the Coromandel coastline roughly 12 km north of central Puducherry. Characterized by wide sloping sands and soft waves, it offers a peaceful respite for long reflective strolls, shells gathering, and sunrise photography.
places.accessNote: Check sea conditions before entering water; rip currents occur seasonally.

places.name: French War Memorial
places.shortDescription: Solemn coastal monument on Goubert Avenue honouring soldiers of the First World War.
places.longDescription: Erected in 1937 on Goubert Avenue facing the Bay of Bengal, the French War Memorial pays homage to the native and French residents of French India who gave their lives during the First World War. It is beautifully illuminated each year on Bastille Day (14 July).
places.accessNote: Viewable from beachfront walkway; interior ceremonial grounds open during official commemorations.

places.name: Mahatma Gandhi Statue
places.shortDescription: Four-metre bronze statue framed by eight ornate monolithic granite pillars from Gingee Fort.
places.longDescription: The Mahatma Gandhi Statue is an iconic landmark standing at the centre of Promenade Beach. The four-metre-high bronze sculpture is surrounded by eight majestic monolithic carved granite pillars brought from the 17th-century Gingee Fort, with an open amphitheatre hosting cultural events.
places.accessNote: Pedestrian area along Goubert Avenue; wheelchair accessible.

places.name: Aayi Mandapam (Bharathi Park)
places.shortDescription: White Greco-Roman pavilion in Bharathi Park honoring a generous local woman of 16th-century legend.
places.longDescription: Standing at the center of Bharathi Park, Aayi Mandapam is a striking white Greco-Roman pavilion built during the reign of Napoleon III. It commemorates Aayi, a 16th-century courtesan who gave her water reservoir to provide clean drinking water to the city during a severe drought.
places.accessNote: Located inside Bharathi Park; park closes at sunset.

places.name: Old Lighthouse
places.shortDescription: 19th-century French colonial maritime tower overlooking Goubert Avenue and the Bay of Bengal.
places.longDescription: Built by French engineer Louis Guerre in 1836, the Old Lighthouse first shone its beam across the Coromandel coast on 1 July 1836. Located across Goubert Avenue near Place de la République, this 29-metre circular fluted stone tower remains an enduring symbol of maritime history.
places.accessNote: Check current interior access before planning entry; exterior fully viewable.

places.name: Raj Niwas (Governor's Palace)
places.shortDescription: Stately 18th-century French neoclassical palace, official residence of the Lieutenant Governor.
places.longDescription: Raj Niwas is the official residence of the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry. Originally the French Governor-General's palace, its architecture blends classic French colonial style with high ceilings and spacious verandas facing Bharathi Park.
places.accessNote: Interior access restricted to designated public visiting slots; exterior viewable from perimeter.

places.name: Arulmigu Manakula Vinayagar Temple
places.shortDescription: Ancient Ganesha temple predating French colonial arrival with ornate golden chariot.
places.longDescription: Arulmigu Manakula Vinayagar Temple is a revered Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Ganesha, founded prior to the arrival of the French in 1673. Famous for its gilded vimanam, ornate painted mythological frescoes depicting Ganesha's pastimes, and a ceremonial gold-plated temple chariot.
whatToExperience: Carved stone pillars and golden shrine
places.accessNote: Footwear must be deposited outside; respectful temple attire covering shoulders and knees.

places.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
places.shortDescription: Magnificent Gothic Revival basilica featuring 28 rare stained-glass biblical portraits.
places.longDescription: Consecrated in 1907 by French missionaries, the Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus is an oriental Gothic marvel on South Boulevard. Featuring twin bell towers, corinthian columns, Latin inscriptions, and rare stained-glass windows detailing the life of Jesus Christ.
whatToExperience: Historic pipe organ and choir loft
places.accessNote: Quiet sanctuary; respectful modest clothing required.

places.name: Église de Notre Dame des Anges
places.shortDescription: Pastel pink and cream Greco-Roman church with limestone-egg mortar facing the sea.
places.longDescription: Modeled after the Basilica at Lourdes and completed in 1855, Église de Notre Dame des Anges stands along Rue Dumas overlooking the ocean. Built with limestone mixed with egg whites for an enduring marble-like sheen, it is the only church in Puducherry where mass is celebrated in French, Tamil, and English.
whatToExperience: Statue of Joan of Arc in garden square
places.accessNote: Modest attire required inside the church nave.

places.name: Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception
aliases: Eglise de Notre Dame de la Conception Immortelle
places.shortDescription: Historic 300-year-old mother church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Pondicherry.
places.longDescription: The Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception on Mission Street is the mother church of the Archdiocese of Puducherry and Cuddalore. Built in classical Jesuit-Portuguese style in 1791 over earlier 17th-century foundations, it features a grand courtyard and ornate bell tower.
whatToExperience: High altar with statues of Saints
places.accessNote: Located on Cathedral Street / Mission Street; quiet atmosphere.

places.name: Vedapureeswarar Temple
places.shortDescription: Historic Shiva temple in Heritage Town with 75-foot Raja Gopuram.
places.longDescription: Vedapureeswarar Temple is a historic temple dedicated to Lord Shiva situated along Mahatma Gandhi Road. Rebuilt in the late 18th century after colonial conflicts, it showcases classic Dravidian stone carvings, a tall seven-tiered gopuram, and sacred Shiva lingam.
places.accessNote: Remove footwear before entry; non-Hindus welcome in outer courtyards.

places.name: Thirukameswarar Temple, Villianur
places.shortDescription: Ancient 12th-century Chola Shiva temple located in Villianur with sacred spring-fed tank.
places.longDescription: Located approximately 10 km west of central Puducherry in Villianur, Thirukameswarar Temple was constructed during the Chola era under King Kulothunga I. It features magnificent stone pillars, ancient Tamil epigraphs, and a large spring-fed sacred tank celebrated for its annual temple car festival.
places.accessNote: Check bus or auto connectivity from Puducherry bus stand.

places.name: Kanniga Parameswari Temple
places.shortDescription: Unique temple combining French architraves and ionic pillars with Dravidian sanctum art.
places.longDescription: Located on MG Road in Heritage Town, this temple dedicated to Goddess Shakti is notable for its rare Indo-French architectural fusion: the exterior displays stained-glass clerestories and European ionic columns, while the inner sanctum follows orthodox Dravidian agamic design.
places.accessNote: Active worship place; verify exact daily festival hours.

places.name: Meeran Mosque
places.shortDescription: Historic 350-year-old Gothic-Islamic mosque in Heritage Town.
places.longDescription: Constructed over 350 years ago in the early days of Puducherry, Meeran Mosque showcases distinct Gothic-Islamic archways, fluted bronze minarets, and tranquil prayer halls in the Tamil Quarter.
places.accessNote: Dress modestly; verify prayer visiting times.

places.name: Kuthba Mosque
places.shortDescription: One of the oldest documented mosques in central Puducherry.
places.longDescription: The Kuthba Mosque is historically one of the earliest Muslim houses of prayer established in the town center, featuring classic arched prayer pavilions and historical tombs.
places.accessNote: Verify visiting guidelines.

places.name: Jamia Mosque
places.shortDescription: Prominent central mosque in the Muslim quarter with open prayer courtyard.
places.longDescription: The Jamia Mosque serves as the central Friday congregational mosque of Puducherry, located within the historic Tamil Muslim quarter with a spacious open-air courtyard.
places.accessNote: Modest attire required.

places.name: Bharathi Park (Government Park)
places.shortDescription: Tranquil central green space surrounded by Raj Niwas and the High Court.
places.longDescription: Bharathi Park is the green heart of the French Quarter, laid out in the 19th century with manicured lawns, mature shade trees, play areas, and the iconic white Aayi Mandapam monument situated at its centre.
whatToExperience: Shady walking paths under ancient trees
places.accessNote: Open to public daily; closes at sunset.

places.name: Botanical Garden
places.shortDescription: 22-acre historic French colonial garden founded in 1826 with over 1,500 botanical species.
places.longDescription: Established in 1826 by French botanist C.S. Perrottet, the Botanical Garden features 22 acres of rare flora, ancient mahogany trees, a musical fountain, and a toy train. The ornate entrance gate exemplifies classic French colonial garden design.
places.accessNote: Wheelchair accessible pathways; toy train operates select hours.

places.name: Jawahar Toy Museum
places.shortDescription: Quaint museum near the Old Lighthouse exhibiting traditional dolls and toys from Indian states.
places.longDescription: Located next to the Old Lighthouse on Goubert Avenue, the Jawahar Toy Museum displays over 120 dolls dressed in customary regional costumes from states across India, illustrating traditional handicraft diversity.
places.accessNote: Check current opening status before visiting; renovations occur periodically.

places.name: Chunnambar Boat House
places.shortDescription: Popular backwater recreational center and ferry boarding point for Paradise Beach.
places.longDescription: Located 8 km south of Puducherry along the Cuddalore Road, Chunnambar Boat House is situated where the Chunnambar River joins the Bay of Bengal. It offers motorboat cruises, pedal boats, and the official passenger ferry to Paradise Beach.
places.accessNote: Boat ticket queue can be busy on weekends; wear life jackets on all boat trips.

places.name: Ousteri Wetland and National Park
places.shortDescription: Century-old freshwater wetland and designated bird sanctuary hosting migratory avifauna.
places.longDescription: Ousteri Lake is an expansive 800-hectare freshwater wetland recognized as an Important Bird Area (IBA). Located 10 km northwest of Puducherry, it hosts over 40 species of migratory birds including openbill storks, painted storks, and egrets.
places.accessNote: Best visited with own transport; binoculars recommended.

places.name: Arikamedu Archaeological Site
places.shortDescription: Ancient Indo-Roman maritime port and archaeological site on the Ariyankuppam River.
places.longDescription: Arikamedu is a legendary ancient port town dating from the 2nd century BCE to the 2nd century CE. Excavations led by Sir Mortimer Wheeler revealed Roman amphorae, gems, glassware, and beads, proving thriving trade links between ancient Tamil kingdoms and Imperial Rome.
places.accessNote: Open archaeological grounds; limited signage; best visited in morning.

places.name: Auroville Visitors Centre
places.shortDescription: Information hub for Auroville with photo galleries, video screenings, eco-boutiques, and cafes.
places.longDescription: The Auroville Visitors Centre serves as the welcoming entry point to the international township of Auroville. Built with compressed earth blocks, it features informational exhibitions on the township's philosophy, pass registration for Matrimandir viewing, handicraft boutiques, and organic cafes.
whatToExperience: Eco-friendly handmade paper and pottery boutiques
places.accessNote: Obtain Matrimandir viewing passes here in person.

places.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Statue
places.shortDescription: Seafront statue of India's first Prime Minister facing the Gandhi memorial on Goubert Avenue.
places.longDescription: Standing along the northern stretch of Goubert Avenue across from the French Consulate, this bronze statue commemorates Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, who described Pondicherry as 'the window of French culture'.
places.accessNote: Located along pedestrian promenade.

places.name: Dupleix Statue
places.shortDescription: Historical bronze statue of French Governor Joseph François Dupleix at the southern promenade.
places.longDescription: Erected in honour of Joseph François Dupleix, Governor-General of French establishments in India from 1742 to 1754, this 2.88-metre bronze statue stands in a landscaped park at the southern tip of Goubert Avenue.
places.accessNote: Public seafront garden.

places.name: Romain Rolland Library
places.shortDescription: One of the oldest functioning public libraries in India, established in 1827.
places.longDescription: Established in 1827, the Romain Rolland Library on Rue Rangapillai houses a collection of over 300,000 volumes, including priceless rare French manuscripts, early editions, and regional historical journals.
places.accessNote: Silence must be observed; photo restrictions in archive rooms.

places.name: French Institute of Pondicherry (IFP)
places.shortDescription: Premier Indology and scientific research institute founded in 1955 on Saint Louis Street.
places.longDescription: Founded under the 1954 Franco-Indian treaty, the French Institute of Pondicherry is a world-renowned research institute housing extensive collections of palm-leaf manuscripts, South Indian temple photo archives, and botanical palynology collections.
whatToExperience: Colonial architecture along Rue Saint Louis
places.accessNote: Public access may be limited; inquire at entrance for public exhibitions.

places.name: Alliance Française de Pondichéry
places.shortDescription: Vibrant French cultural centre on Rue Suffren with art gallery, cinema, and cafe.
places.longDescription: Established in 1889 as one of the first Alliance Française branches in the world, this vibrant cultural center hosts French language courses, contemporary art exhibitions, indie film screenings, and live music performances.
places.accessNote: Check current programme schedule for open public art shows.

places.name: Hotel de Ville / Municipal Office
places.shortDescription: Historic 19th-century French civic town hall rebuilt along Goubert Avenue.
places.longDescription: The Hotel de Ville (Town Hall), built in 1870 along Goubert Avenue, originally housed the mayor's office and civic assembly. Faithfully reconstructed after a heritage conservation effort, its arched windows and French pediments grace the promenade.
places.accessNote: Exterior viewable from promenade.

places.name: Old Port / Old Harbour Area
places.shortDescription: Historic 284-metre iron shipping pier remnants from 1862.
places.longDescription: Built in 1862, the historic Old Pier was a 284-metre iron structure that served as the primary cargo lifeline for French merchant ships visiting Pondicherry. The weathered iron pilings and coastal seawall stand as an evocative maritime relic.
whatToExperience: Historic iron pier pilings in crashing waves
places.accessNote: Access varies depending on coastal surf and municipal works.

places.name: Auroville Farms & Green Belt
places.shortDescription: Lush reforestation belt with organic spirulina, dairy, and regenerative permaculture farms.
places.longDescription: Surrounding Auroville is a vibrant green belt created over five decades through planting over three million trees. It houses organic farms, seed banks, and community food-forest projects pioneering sustainable soil regeneration.
places.accessNote: Some farm visits require prior arrangement with Auroville Visitors Centre.

places.name: Karaikal Beach
places.shortDescription: Wide sandy beach in the Karaikal enclave, roughly 130 km south of central Puducherry.
places.longDescription: Karaikal Beach is located in Karaikal, an outlying district of the Union Territory of Puducherry situated 130 km to the south along the Arasalar River delta. It features wide tranquil sands, a sea promenade, and family park.
places.accessNote: Located roughly 130 km from Puducherry city; requires multi-hour train or road journey.
